capitalisedCommonWords.description: tier-d words the name stage found no Hebrew name for, tagged from their lower-case readings (capitals.py)

misprints.description: printed forms read as another word because text.MISPRINT_TABLE lists them as misprints of the digitised text; the text itself is unchanged

methods.hebrew-association: the Hebrew name the verses of an untagged Greek form nearly always have and no other Greek word of them accounts for (names no transliteration finds)
methods.hebrew-consistency: the number the same Greek form takes everywhere it is matched
methods.hebrew-nearby: matched to a name of a neighbouring Hebrew verse, or of the same chapter
methods.hebrew-order: placed by a list's order between matched names of that verse
methods.hebrew-verse: matched to a name of the Hebrew verse the Septuagint's verse corresponds to

relations.description: transliterates: the Greek word reads as the Hebrew name it is tagged with; stands-for: the Septuagint prints another name at that position and the tag says which Hebrew name it stands for: found by association, or a reading below the verse threshold that is very poor or that another name of the chapter reads better, or a form that elsewhere renders another Hebrew name it reads better (names.name_relations)

names.sourceNote: Proper names the New Testament does not use are identified from STEPBible's tagged Hebrew Old Testament (TAHOT and TBESH, CC BY 4.0): each carries the Strong's number of the Hebrew name it renders in the same verse.

tierD.note: candidates include capitalised tier-e words (see tierE)

tierDescriptions.b: one Strong's number and lemma, several parses
tierDescriptions.d: looks like a name, no acceptable candidate
tierDescriptions.u: unconfirmed: tolerant match only, or names for a lower-case word

tolerantNameParses.description: names tagged from a loose match with an NT name: the rule that read their case from the Septuagint word (name_parse.py), or unknown (the NT form's parse kept, its confidence capped)
